### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Neovim version

0.12 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

I want B to search using the search method I specified in the config

### Reproduction

```lua
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()
    require('mini.ai').setup ({
      custom_textobjects = {
	b = false,
      },
      search_method = 'next',
    })
```

- Use the config above
- Create a new lua file with this example code: 
```lua
local xyz = {
   zzz = 1,
   |yyy = {   -- PUT THE CURSOR IN THIS LINE
     xxx = 2,
  }
}
```
- With the cursor in the third line as specified above, now type `ciB`
- This is the result:
```lua
local xyz = {
  | -- CURSOR IS HERE
}
```

- Since I specified search_method = 'next', I would have expected this result instead
```lua
local xyz = {
   zzz = 1,
   yyy = {
     | -- CURSOR IS HERE
  }
}
```

Something interesting is that running `ci{` instead of `ciB` works perfectly

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

The config you provided doesn't have `B` textobject set up and it is [not a built-in one](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/77e20cd6ed80fdf1738c116c35da81e7d9ad997e/doc/mini-ai.txt#L137-L170). The config only disables `b` textobject, so something like `cib` will use built-in `ib` textobject and not the 'mini.ai' one.

---

I would also suggest to not use `'next'` as a global search method, as it won't find covering textobjects (which is the most common use case, I'd say). Try setting `'cover'` as global search method and then use explicit `an` and `in` to search with `'next'` search method. Like `cin)` (search with `'next'`) instead of `ci)` (search with global `'cover'`).

@echasnovski Thank you for you quick answer, here are my thoughts:

> The config you provided doesn't have `B` textobject set up and it is [not a built-in one](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/77e20cd6ed80fdf1738c116c35da81e7d9ad997e/doc/mini-ai.txt#L137-L170). The config only disables `b` textobject, so something like `cib` will use built-in `ib` textobject and not the 'mini.ai' one.

In neovim documentation `:h text-objects` it says that `b` is just an alias for parenthesis `()` and capital `B` is an alias for `{}` so I think this behavior should be covered by default in this plugin, it's confusing that some text-objects have some behavior and others don't.

> I would also suggest to not use `'next'` as a global search method, as it won't find covering textobjects (which is the most common use case, I'd say). Try setting `'cover'` as global search method and then use explicit `an` and `in` to search with `'next'` search method. Like `cin)` (search with `'next'`) instead of `ci)` (search with global `'cover'`).

I don't like any of the current search methods, I would like it to first, analyze the line where the cursor is placed. I believe there should be an option `line_or_cover`

Just like the vim default `"` text-object 

for example:

```lua
|  local z = "SOME STRING"; -- CURSOR IS AT THE START OF THE LINE
```

If you do at the start of the line `ci"` it will cut the string in the line as expected.

result:
```lua
  local z = "|"; -- CURSOR IS AT THE START OF THE LINE
```

So I think there there should be a search_method that first look in the line where the cursor is, and then if there's no text-object in the line it should search in cover.

I think these two changes are important to try to imitate vim default behaviors. I hope you consider re-opening this issue 🙏

> In neovim documentation `:h text-objects` it says that `b` is just an alias for parenthesis `()` and capital `B` is an alias for `{}` so I think this behavior should be covered by default in this plugin, it's confusing that some text-objects have some behavior and others don't.

Yes, I know that. I don't think it is a good idea to have duplicating textobjects just for the sake of being closer to defaults. If users like that, they can configure both `b` and `B` textobjects to be the same as `[` / `]` and `{` / `}`.

> So I think there there should be a search_method that first look in the line where the cursor is, and then if there's no text-object in the line it should search in cover.

This is almost exactly how `'cover_or_next'` in 'mini.ai' works and [is documented](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/77e20cd6ed80fdf1738c116c35da81e7d9ad997e/doc/mini-ai.txt#L375-L377). There is an "almost" because it also in the end tries to search for the next textobject in the whole neighborhood.

In particular for the described case the following steps are done in order:
- Try to find covering textobject in current line.
- Try to find next textobject in current line.
- Try to find covering textobject within neighborhood (plus and minus 50 lines by default).
- Try to find next textobject within neighborhood.

> I did `ci{` and instead of cutting the `{}` that's in the current line it deleted the one that is covering

The difference is that this `{}` is not *in* the current line, but only starts at it. For such cases (and instead of the default `'cover_or_next'`, really) the recommended way is to `cin{`. Using `{` identifier does "or even better" case, while `}` identifier does "I would have expected this" case.

@echasnovski I've been using this plugin and I found some weird behaviors like this:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49ad58ed-ca49-430d-93cb-f37bc91f4320

As you can see in the video, sometimes doing `ci}` in the same line will work, sometimes it wont. The first time I run `ci}` it deleted the next `{}` not the one in the line. The second time I did `ci}` after deleting some code and It worked. Totally unexpected.

> The difference is that this {} is not in the current line, but only starts at it.

I just can't get my head around this plugin. Some cases it works others it doesn't. There are no clear rules to me... But I guess it's because of treesitter....

> As you can see in the video, sometimes doing `ci}` in the same line will work, sometimes it wont. The first time I run `ci}` it deleted the next `{}` not the one in the line. The second time I did `ci}` after deleting some code and It worked. Totally unexpected.

Assuming it is a demo with `"cover_or_next"` search method (which is default), my guess is that the first time the `{}` "under cursor" spans more than 50 lines. This is a default value of [`config.n_lines`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/77e20cd6ed80fdf1738c116c35da81e7d9ad997e/doc/mini-ai.txt#L450-L451) which limits text used to search for a textobject (for performance reasons). If that is the case, then it works totally expected and as documented in the same link I provided in [this comment](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1905#issuecomment-3102512785). Here is the relevant part describing the search process:

>  Note: first search is done inside reference region lines, and only after that - inside its neighborhood within `config.n_lines` (see |MiniAi.config|).

So the the first `ci}` performs like this:
- Is there a balanced `{}` completely within current line that covers cursor? No.
- Is there a balanced `{}` completely within current line that is after cursor? No.
- Is there a balanced `{}` completely within 50 lines of cursor and covering it? *No*, because the `{}` at which cursor is located probably spans more than 50 lines.
- Is there a balanced `{}` completely within 50 lines of cursor and after it? *Yes*, the one on the next line.

The second time it performs the same steps, but stops at third one.

What you can do here is increase `n_lines` to a comfortably big value and see if the behavior changes.

> I just can't get my head around this plugin. Some cases it works others it doesn't. There are no clear rules to me... But I guess it's because of treesitter....

The `}` textobjects doesn't rely on tree-sitter. And I assure you, the chance that built-in non-tree-sitter textobject has "some cases it works others it doesn't" is very small. There are a lot of tests covering many edge cases which cover clear and documented rules.

title: Capital B in mini.ai doesn't respect search_method
